name: Question 4
problem:
Consider the inhomogeneous system  ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+g(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix. A derivation of the formula for the solution $x(t)$ passing through $x(0)$ is presented below.

$\text{L1}:\,$ Let $y(t)={e}^{-At}x(t)$  

$\text{L2}:\,$ ${y}^{′}(t)=-A{e}^{-At}x(t)+{e}^{-At}{x}^{′}(t)$  

$\text{L3}:\,$ ${y}^{′}(t)={e}^{-At}g(t)$  

$\text{L4}:\,$ $y(t)-y(0)={\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{-As}g(s)\,\text{d}s$

$\text{L5}:\,$ $y(0)=x(0)$ 

$\text{L6}:\,$ $y(t)=x(0)+{\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{-As}g(s)\,\text{d}s$  

$\text{L7}:\,$ ${e}^{At}y(t)={e}^{At}x(0)+{\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s$

$\text{L8}:\,$ ${e}^{At}y(t)=x(t)$

$\text{L9}:\,$ $x(t)={e}^{At}x(0)+{\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s$

Select the correct options to justify each step of the reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L2}$ follows from $\text{L1}$ by  
{{field-1}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L6}$ follows from line
{{field-2}}
by substituting 
{{field-3}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L9}$ follows from line $\text{L7}$ by  
{{field-4}}.
worked_solution:
Let's justify each of the selected steps.

- We first consider lines $\text{L1}$ and $\text{L2}.$ Differentiating $y(t)={e}^{-At}x(t)$ and applying the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(t) & =({e}^{-At})^{′}x(t)+{e}^{-At}{x}^{′}(t) \\  & =(-A){e}^{-At}x(t)+{e}^{-At}{x}^{′}(t) \\  & =-A{e}^{-At}x(t)+{e}^{-At}{x}^{′}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $\text{L2}$ follows from $\text{L1}$ by $\text{differentiating and using the product rule}.$

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L4}$, $\text{L5}$, and $\text{L6}.$ From $\text{L4}$ we have

$$
y(t)-y(0)={\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{-As}g(s)\,\text{d}s.
$$

Using $y(0)=x(0)$ from $\text{L5}$, this becomes

$$
y(t)-x(0)={\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{-As}g(s)\,\text{d}s,
$$

so

$$
y(t)=x(0)+{\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{-As}g(s)\,\text{d}s.
$$

Thus, $\text{L6}$ follows from $\text{L4}$ by substituting $y(0)=x(0).$

- Finally, we consider lines $\text{L7}$, $\text{L8}$, and $\text{L9}.$ From $\text{L8}$ we know that

$$
{e}^{At}y(t)=x(t).
$$

Substituting ${e}^{At}y(t)=x(t)$ into

$$
{e}^{At}y(t)={e}^{At}x(0)+{\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s
$$

from $\text{L7}$ gives

$$
x(t)={e}^{At}x(0)+{\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s.
$$

Therefore, $\text{L9}$ follows from $\text{L7}$ by $\text{substituting }{e}^{At}y(t)=x(t).$

Question 4
?
Consider the inhomogeneous system x′(t)=Ax(t)+g(t), where A is a constant square matrix. A derivation of the formula for the solution x(t) passing through x(0) is presented below.

L1: Let y(t)=e−Atx(t)

L2: y′(t)=−Ae−Atx(t)+e−Atx′(t)

L3: y′(t)=e−Atg(t)

L4: y(t)−y(0)=∫0te−Asg(s)ds

L5: y(0)=x(0)

L6: y(t)=x(0)+∫0te−Asg(s)ds

L7: eAty(t)=eAtx(0)+∫0teA(t−s)g(s)ds

L8: eAty(t)=x(t)

L9: x(t)=eAtx(0)+∫0teA(t−s)g(s)ds

Select the correct options to justify each step of the reasoning.

Line L2 follows from L1 by
differentiating and using the product rule
applying a change of variables
differentiating and using the product rule
evaluating at t=0
substituting x′(t)=Ax(t)+g(t)
.

Line L6 follows from line
L4
L1
L3
L4
by substituting
y(0)=x(0)
eAty(t)=x(t)
y(t)=e−Atx(t)
y(0)=x(0)
x′(t)=Ax(t)+g(t)
.

Line L9 follows from line L7 by
substituting eAty(t)=x(t)
substituting eAty(t)=x(t)
multiplying both sides by eAt
applying a change of variables
evaluating at t=0
.
Submit

EXPLANATION

Let's justify each of the selected steps.

  • We first consider lines L1 and L2. Differentiating y(t)=e−Atx(t) and applying the product rule gives
    y′(t)=(e−At)′x(t)+e−Atx′(t)=(−A)e−Atx(t)+e−Atx′(t)=−Ae−Atx(t)+e−Atx′(t). Thus, L2 follows from L1 by differentiating and using the product rule.

  • Next, we consider lines L4, L5, and L6. From L4 we have y(t)−y(0)=∫0te−Asg(s)ds. Using y(0)=x(0) from L5, this becomes
    y(t)−x(0)=∫0te−Asg(s)ds, so y(t)=x(0)+∫0te−Asg(s)ds. Thus, L6 follows from L4 by substituting y(0)=x(0).

  • Finally, we consider lines L7, L8, and L9. From L8 we know that eAty(t)=x(t). Substituting eAty(t)=x(t) into eAty(t)=eAtx(0)+∫0teA(t−s)g(s)ds from L7 gives
    x(t)=eAtx(0)+∫0teA(t−s)g(s)ds. Therefore, L9 follows from L7 by substituting eAty(t)=x(t).
